newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in trendless trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in trendless trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Thursday in trendless trade as investors took profits on Wednesday's run-up, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.14 percent, or 0.42 points, to 296.39 on all-share turnover of 208 million shekels against 308 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.09 percent lower at 305.54.

"This is the calm after the storm," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance. "It was a very active and tense week, with lots of rumours and speculation that reached a peak on Wednesday. Now we need to calm down".

Israeli shares rallied on Wednesday in response to a sharp cut in the Bank of Israel's key lending rate by 1.2 percentage point to an annualised 12.7 percent and the cabinet's adoption of a foreign currency reform package.
"I think that it's a positive sign that after such an active day (on Wednesday) the market relaxes with only a mild decline rather than a strong correction," Glicksberg said.
Glicksberg said the decline in interest rates over the last year from a peak of 17 percent represented a clear trend that was likely to continue. "It adds to investor confidence," he said.
"People are looking for a reason to buy and the interest rate cut is a good reason. Foreigners have been active lately," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Securities.

But Danni Scharia of Capital Securities said investors would need some time to digest the other changes. "We still do not know who is going to be the next finance minister and how will the forex market react to the reform," he said.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor quit on Wednesday after the currency reforms were adopted by the cabinet in a hastily arranged night session.

Bank Leumi led the most active shares by a wide margin, climbing 1.75 percent to 583 agorot on turnover of 23.7 million shekels. No. 2 Israel Discount Bank rose 2.75 percent to 407 agorot on volume of 8.5 million shekels and No. 3 Bank Hapoalim gained 0.5 percent to 805 agorot on volume of 7.5 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
